title: Miss Medicare Enrollment at 65 and the Penalty Isn’t a Fine. It’s a Higher Premium for Life.
excerpt: Missing Medicare's enrollment window does not trigger a one-time fine you pay and move on from. It attaches a surcharge to your monthly premium that compound...
content_html:
David Beren

Wed, August 5, 2026 at 12:10 PM CDT 5 min read

Quick Read

  • Missing Medicare's 7-month enrollment window triggers a permanent Part B surcharge of 10% per year delayed, riding every future premium increase for life.

  • A two-year delay raises the 2026 monthly Part B premium from $203 to roughly $243; a five-year delay pushes it above $304.

  • Enrolling during the 7-month birthday window avoids Part B penalties entirely; workers with qualifying employer coverage must file SEP paperwork within 8 months of losing it.

Medicare eligibility begins at age 65, and the sign-up window is short. The Initial Enrollment Period lasts seven months, starting three months before the birthday month and ending three months after. Miss that window without qualifying coverage from a current employer, and the cost is structural: a permanent surcharge added to the monthly premium, adjusted each year upward as premiums rise.

The 2026 Baseline Numbers

The 2026 standard Part B premium, set by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, comes in at $202.90 per month, an increase of $17.90 from $185 in 2025. The annual Part B deductible for 2026 is $283, up from $257. Those are the baseline numbers before any penalty applies. The Part A inpatient hospital deductible is $1,736 in 2026, an increase of $60 from $1,676 in 2025, though roughly 99% of beneficiaries pay no Part A premium because they have at least 40 quarters of Medicare-covered employment.

How the Part B Penalty Actually Works

The Part B late enrollment penalty adds 10% of the standard premium for each full 12-month period a person could have had Part B but did not enroll. That surcharge remains attached to the monthly premium for as long as the person has Part B. Someone who delays for 2 full years pays 20% more every month. Delay five years, and the premium runs 50% above the standard rate.

  • 缺少 Medicare 的 7 个月投保窗口会触发每年延迟 10% 的永久性 B 部分附加费，并终身享受未来保费的每次增加。
  • 两年的延迟将 2026 年 B 部分每月保费从 203 美元提高到约 243 美元；五年的延迟使其突破 304 美元。
  • 在 7 个月生日窗口期间注册可以完全避免 B 部分的处罚；拥有合格雇主保险的工人必须在丢失 SEP 文件后 8 个月内提交该文件。

医疗保险资格从 65 岁开始，并且注册窗口很短。 初始注册期持续七个月，从生日月份前三个月开始，到生日月份后三个月结束。 如果错过了当前雇主没有提供合格保险的窗口，其成本是结构性的：每月保费中会添加永久性附加费，随着保费上涨，每年都会向上调整。

2026 年基准数字

医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心制定的 2026 年标准 B 部分保费为每月 202.90 美元，比 2025 年的 185 美元增加了 17.90 美元。 2026 年 B 部分年度免赔额为 283 美元，高于 257 美元。 这些是任何处罚之前的基线数字。 2026 年 A 部分住院免赔额为 1,736 美元，比 2025 年的 1,676 美元增加了 60 美元，尽管大约 99% 的受益人不支付 A 部分保费，因为他们至少有 40 个季度的医疗保险承保就业。

B 部分处罚的实际运作方式

对于本来可以参加 B 部分但没有参加的人，每满 12 个月，B 部分延迟投保罚款将增加 10% 的标准保费。 只要该人拥有 B 部分，该附加费就一直附加在每月保费中。 拖延 2 年的人每月要多付 20% 的费用。 延迟五年，保费将比标准费率高出 50%。
